trajectory_summary: The call opens hostile-adjacent with a customer actively trying to disqualify herself and stall, and the rep works through each block with quick, concrete answers rather than defensiveness, gradually earning enough trust that she voluntarily engages, sends her bill photo, and books an appointment. The rep's execution is efficient but light — verify questions are rushed through without depth, the bill amount and interest reason are captured but never flipped or reinforced, and the button-up drifts from script language. Ends in a real booked appointment with date/time locked, which is a good outcome given the skeptical opening, but the fragility (unaddressed tree/shading worry, thin qualification depth) is left for the closer to inherit.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Button-up script drift + missing handshake elements
primary_coaching_focus.quote: The only thing they ask is that you're not driving and you're able to access your email.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep substituted 'access your email' for the schema's 'sit down to review the design on your computer' and skipped the one-hour block statement and the 'is that fair?' verbal handshake entirely. These are the mechanics proven to affect show rate, and on a call where the customer was won late and gently, a clean, complete close matters more, not less.

key_moments.quote: I have to think about this. My my son and daughter-in-law had, I guess, it was Duke Power.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a soft stall dressed as a comparison anecdote (free program elsewhere) rather than a hard objection, but it's still an opening to reframe: the free-program story is actually a chance to contrast with Ion's guaranteed-savings bill swap. Rep instead answers narrowly ('Oh, I don't think so') and lets her keep control of the thread toward 'let me talk to my neighbor.'

key_moments.quote: Well because I just billed out estimates and quotes. So if you want, I can help you build one real quick, and then you can just get an offer. You don't even have to make any decisions.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep substitutes a low-commitment ask (build a quote, no decision required) for the harder ask (book now), successfully converting her 'let me ask my neighbor' stall into forward motion.

key_moments.quote: Well, you can see that it has a good many trees in the area that's between us and the sun in the west.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer gives specific, escalating detail about shading (leaves not out yet, tall trees, tall house, neighbor's own shading problem) — a real technical concern, not a stall. Rep's response stays surface-level ('It doesn't look too bad, though') without acknowledging the leaves-not-out timing detail she's flagging as a reason his satellite read may be misleading.

key_moments.quote: I had a, like, a $350 bill. It's usually from $1.50 to $2.50, I think.
key_moments.stewart_read: A strong anchor point — a recent bill spike plus a stated normal range — captured cleanly by the rep ('Okay. So $1.50 to $2.50... Let me put that down'), but never flipped into the bill-swap savings framing already pitched at 01:05.
